questions.question: A week ends on Sunday. Bitcoin traded all weekend; MSTR last traded Friday. Why not use Sunday's BTC price with Friday's MSTR price?
options: m = s / (p·n) would compare two different moments, and the weekend coin move would show up in m with no action behind it
MSTR's Friday close already includes Sunday's BTC price
questions.explanation: Every ticker in a week uses the same price date, so p, s and q describe one moment.

questions.question: What is Yahoo's adjclose series?
options: The last trade before the close
The close back-adjusted for dividends and splits, which changes after the fact
The average of open and close
The close in the exchange's time zone
questions.explanation: Adjusted closes are rewritten when a dividend is paid. The preferreds here pay large dividends, so the project uses the quote close to keep past q values fixed.

questions.question: data/prices.csv has no MSTR close on Friday 2026-06-19. Which BTC close does weekly.csv use for Strategy's week ending 2026-06-21?
questions.explanation: The price date is the last MSTR close on or before the week end: 2026-06-18. BTC is looked up at that same date.

questions.question: Which CoinGecko point is the BTC close for 2026-05-25?
questions.explanation: The close for day D is the point at 00:00 UTC on D+1, about 4 hours after the US equity close. tests/test_prices.py pins exactly this case.

questions.question: STRC closed at $88.59 on the price date. What is q?
questions.explanation: q for STRC = STRC close / 100, its stated amount per share: 88.59 / 100 = 0.8859, the value in weekly.csv.
